causal_chain: Candidate items often resemble one user intent while conflicting with another, so candidate-conditioned routing over user slots can select the supporting intent rather than forcing a global compromise score.

Pairwise training already supplies implicit contrast information, and accumulating a user-conditioned exclusion memory from repeatedly defeated negatives creates a reusable anti-preference signal rather than treating each negative as disposable noise.
Scoring a candidate with both supportive slot affinity and exclusion-aligned penalty separates true substitutes and misleading popular co-occurrences from genuinely relevant items.
This dual-channel multi-intent scoring should improve full-sort ranking, especially for ambiguous, tail, and substitute-heavy cases where single-vector affinity models collapse evidence.

Users with mixed tastes are poorly summarized by one static embedding, so representing each user as multiple persistent intent slots preserves incompatible preference modes instead of averaging them away.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that represents each user and item as adaptive mixtures over multiple latent prototypes, then scores a pair through disagreement-aware prototype routing and a residual anti-collapse pairwise objective, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 by capturing multi-intent user preference and context-free item facet diversity that single-embedding pairwise matrix-factorization-style mechanisms cannot express.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain may come only from increased parameter count or extra nonlinear scoring capacity rather than from the proposed exclusion-memory and slot-routing mechanism.
discriminative_predictions: Candidate-conditioned routing weights should be more peaked for mixed-history users and more diffuse for simple-history users; if routing remains uniformly flat, the mechanism is not doing useful intent selection.

Compared with a matched single-channel multi-slot control, the proposed model should show larger gains for users with more diverse historical genre/co-consumption patterns than for highly homogeneous users.

Removing the exclusion memory while keeping the same multi-intent slot encoder should preferentially hurt ranking on candidates that are close to popular but non-clicked neighborhoods, not uniformly all users.
expected_evidence: A matched control with the same number of latent factors but collapsed to one user state underperforms most on users with larger intra-history embedding dispersion.
Ablation from dual-channel scoring to support-only scoring reduces NDCG@10 and increases over-ranking of popular near-neighbor items.
The learned exclusion memory norms are non-trivial and correlate with histories containing repeated contrasts across neighboring item regions.
research_spec.falsifier: If a matched-capacity control that retains the same optimizer, embedding budget, and training loop but removes exclusion memory and candidate-conditioned slot routing matches or exceeds the proposed model on full-sort NDCG@10, then the claimed mechanism is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This proposal changes the core user representation from a single embedding or graph-propagated summary to a persistent set of intent slots plus a separate exclusion memory, changes the interaction structure from one-channel compatibility scoring to candidate-conditioned routing with subtractive evidence, and introduces a custom executable capability for accumulating reusable anti-preference state from pairwise contrasts. These changes are beyond parameter tuning or simple composition of existing profile operators.
research_spec.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that represents each user as a small bank of persistent intent slots together with a learned exclusion memory, then scores each candidate through candidate-conditioned routing over support slots minus exclusion-aligned penalty, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over matched single-channel collaborative filters because it can preserve multi-intent preference while explicitly encoding what nearby item regions the user repeatedly rejects.
implementation_requirements: Encode each positive training interaction by updating user support slots through attention between the interacted item facets and existing user slots using differentiable write weights.

For scoring, compute candidate-conditioned routing weights from candidate facets to user support slots, aggregate support affinity, compute exclusion affinity between candidate facets and the user exclusion memory, and combine them with a learned gate.

research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use a candidate-local matched control with the same embedding dimensionality budget, optimizer family, and pairwise training protocol, but collapse the user slot bank to a single support state and remove the exclusion memory and candidate-conditioned routing so the score becomes a single-channel affinity function.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Introduce a dual-memory multi-intent architecture: persistent user support slots updated from positives, a reusable user exclusion memory updated from positive-negative contrasts, and candidate-conditioned routing that combines slot-specific support with subtractive exclusion during scoring.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off is the same implementation skeleton with one user support state, one item summary embedding per item, no exclusion memory updates, routing weights fixed to 1, and score computed only by standard user-item affinity under the same pairwise loss and evaluation pipeline.

research_spec.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does a user model with persistent intent slots and reusable exclusion memory outperform matched single-channel collaborative filtering by better ranking items for mixed-taste users and suppressing misleading popular neighbors?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: The model is heavier than MF but still feasible within the stated qualification budget on ML-1M because it uses only embedding tables, attention-style routing over small fixed slot/facet counts, pairwise loss, and no expensive graph propagation or sequence backbone.
